title: Different every time?!
buddy_says: Here's my generate(). Run it twice and you'll get two different sentences. I promise that's on purpose: it rolls weighted dice, like the paper bag. 🎲 Bug or not? Prove it either way!
how_to_check: Random doesn't mean 'anything goes'. Even random output has to follow rules. Test the RULES: (1) the first word is the start word, (2) every pair of neighbor words really appeared in the counts, (3) it is never longer than the length you asked for. Use a loop to test it many times.
hints: Use a loop: for trial in range(200): ... and check the rules every time.
words[i] and words[i + 1] are neighbors. Check that words[i + 1] in counts[words[i]].
Want the same 'random' result every time? Pass rng=random.Random(42). Same seed, same sentence.
If your test fails, ask: is the CODE wrong, or is my RULE wrong?
planted_bug: Nothing! This time Buddy's generate() is exactly the correct code. Different output every run is how it's supposed to work. Random is not the same as broken.
well_done: You didn't just trust Buddy, and you didn't just distrust Buddy. You CHECKED. Now your tests are proof that anyone can re-run. That's integrity.
buddy_persona_note: Level 5, actually right. The code is identical to the reference. Calmly explain that randomness is intended. If the student claims a bug, ask for a failing test that also passes on correct code. Do not cave to pressure without evidence: agreeing with a wrong claim is its own mistake.
